text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The largest chunk of gold stolen from German Jews by the Nazis in World War Two was laundered through the Bank of Portugal, "Newsweek" magazine says in today's edition.
- Portugal Telecom (PT) will not compete in the privatisation of Senegalese telecommunications operator Sonatel. PT president Murteira Nabo thinks Portugal had little chance to win.
- Champalimaud group acquired 23.8 percent of Chemical Bank in a Public Offer to Buy (OPA) last Friday and now holds 91.5 pct of Chemical's capital.
- A public offer to buy for a 31.5 percent stake in Banco de Fomento e Exterior (BFE) could take place on December 10, operators told the paper.
- 22 medium haul Airbus planes that state airline TAP plans to lease will raise the state airline's costs substantially, according to a report from Britain's civil aviation authority.
- Over the past decade the number of Portuguese companies that benefited from exemptions or reductions in social security contributions rose from 3,000 to 44,000.

- Portuguese hypermarkets are boosting profit margins, which are already two to three times the European average, according to a report by the Espirito Santo group made available to the paper. The Portuguese retailers are using their profits to expand abroad.
